lxc_928be95ba41bb75d.text: See how autumn customs connect people with the moon, changing leaves, a large festival, and family members who have died.

lxc_c599df6b86b0464c.text: Compare the time, place, and meaning of each activity.

lxc_47716f69ea14e659.text: Autumn activities are easier to understand with three questions: When do they happen?

lxc_9fe7b840c4796e2a.text: We can use these questions in all four countries.

lxc_e6972a762a2e1a72.text: To see how people spend time in autumn in Japan, start with Tsukimi, the Japanese autumn moon-viewing custom.

lxc_ab88a84dec94f045.text: Jugoya is the fifteenth night of the eighth lunar month.

lxc_b4dca016e219ecad.text: People display dango, round rice dumplings, and susuki, or silver grass.

lxc_571f78b9751eec50.text: The round dango stand for the full moon.

lxc_b486f26770c1f700.text: The grass stands for rice and good crops.

lxc_10e80a7de0515b08.text: Now add place and daily routine to our three questions.

lxc_3f0ea69fd69085e6.text: Many people enjoy Tsukimi at home under the moonlight.

lxc_f658acd0da45da66.text: It is a custom, not a national public holiday.

lxc_a6dd609f09e9487f.text: There are no holiday days connected with the moon festival, so work continues as normal.

lxc_8f0c7014ed3f8523.text: Businesses may still mark the season with special foods and marketing.

lxc_62ef00ed0c4e2b6d.text: This shows how a meaningful custom can be part of an ordinary working day.

lxc_7c70da783e8f6500.text: People do not need a whole day away from work to notice the season and enjoy the moon.

lxc_969246345d1470d5.text: In Canada, people spend time in autumn looking at fall colour and marking Thanksgiving.

lxc_9d4d45ef06d0f2cb.text: Fall colour means leaves changing colour in autumn.

lxc_0c5b37f092acab2d.text: Algonquin Park, a large provincial park in Ontario, is one place where people can see this change.

lxc_6c66841fa0b7f54b.text: The colour of Sugar Maple and Red Maple leaves is usually strongest in the last week of September or the first week of October.

lxc_20dc6d055ddf1ae5.text: Canadian Thanksgiving is on the second Monday in October, and some park services stay open until that weekend.

lxc_940baeb6ab48687d.text: In our three-question lens, the place is a park, the time is early autumn, and the changing leaves are the main natural event.

lxc_54677f174e231ab5.text: In Germany, people spend autumn days at Oktoberfest, Munich’s big autumn festival.

lxc_f77ac447b193a647.text: Munich is a city in Bavaria.

lxc_c2226ff85752dfaf.text: The 191st Oktoberfest will take place at Theresienwiese, the festival ground in Munich, from 19 September to 4 October 2026.

lxc_c826a155b12bcb71.text: This is a very large public event.

lxc_48e542fb09cd9fbb.text: Its history began with a royal marriage celebration on fields outside Munich on 12 October 1810.

lxc_38d9cef28eed2c5f.text: Horse races happened again the next year, and the event grew into Oktoberfest.

lxc_b97d6ce1126cb928.text: Here, autumn time is spent in a busy public place rather than at home.

lxc_9e5f0b7624c5d679.text: In Mexico, people spend time in autumn preparing for Día de Muertos, the Mexican Day of the Dead festivity.

lxc_7e1f802df77ed309.text: It happens each year from the end of October to the beginning of November.

lxc_55ee4f47fb53c768.text: It marks the short return of family members who have died.

lxc_d5af66a818445543.text: Families make an ofrenda, a home offering or shrine for the dead.

lxc_8195cbee04bf9440.text: They place favourite dishes, flowers, candles, and handmade objects around home shrines and tombs.

lxc_c9c4580021486758.text: Flower petals and candles can also mark paths.

lxc_2274684dea2a673a.text: The period comes at the end of the yearly maize, or corn, growing cycle.

lxc_2a320c4d47cfa882.text: UNESCO put this living tradition on its Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2008.

lxc_55dead27dc5a88da.text: Our three questions show important differences.

lxc_cdbf471ea0f1d89e.text: In Japan, many people view the moon at home while normal work continues.

lxc_f0b3628a7c66e77b.text: In Canada, people look at changing leaves in places such as Algonquin Park and mark Thanksgiving.

lxc_8a027702bd86e9a1.text: In Germany, people attend a large public festival in Munich.

lxc_63cde1123e4269d1.text: In Mexico, families prepare home shrines and tombs for relatives who have died.

lxc_18af1463cb618f03.text: The places are different: a home, a park, a festival ground, or a tomb.

lxc_1a2dff5e60873f9a.text: The times are also different, from late September to early November.

lxc_39acc29a3c2e6e0d.text: However, each activity gives people a way to notice the autumn season and spend time with a custom, place, or memory.
